clue.text: Wizard work by a bellows mender at Covent Garden?

definitions.text: Wizard work by a bellows mender at Covent Garden?

parts.note: wizard as an adjective means marvellous, like magic; a wizard also works magic
Francis Flute is the bellows-mender among the mechanicals in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream

explanation.surface: A conjuror's handiwork performed by a craftsman in London's theatre district.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the whole stretch after 'Wizard': an opera (a work at Covent Garden, home of London's Royal Opera House) titled with the bellows-mender's own name.
explanation.definitionFit: Mozart's opera Die Zauberflöte is regularly staged at the Royal Opera House in Covent Garden.

clue.text: A sheep is in character as one of three

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: A sheep is cast as one of a trio.
explanation.walkthrough: The three are Dumas's Three Musketeers: Athos, Porthos and the one named here.
explanation.definitionFit: One of Dumas's Three Musketeers, alongside Athos and Porthos.

clue.text: Have mutual effect when the theatre bar's open

explanation.definitionFit: To act on each other; split as inter-act it is the theatre interval, when the bar opens between acts.

clue.text: Is Tim's roof roughly raised by this sort of noise?

indicators.note: roughly suggests the words are handled crudely and their letters thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Is Tim's roof lifted by such a din?
explanation.walkthrough: The S of 'Tim's' counts here: IS TIMS ROOF gives ten letters. 'raised by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The musical direction for very loud playing, so a very loud noise.

clue.text: Lacking the status of Orwell's animals

definitions.text: Lacking the status of Orwell's animals

parts.words: Lacking the status of Orwell's animals
parts.note: in Animal Farm the rule is that all animals are equal, so lacking that status means the opposite

explanation.walkthrough: Orwell's Animal Farm proclaims 'All animals are equal', later adding 'but some animals are more equal than others'.
explanation.definitionFit: Not of the same rank or level, the opposite of equal.

clue.text: Fiery saint, all at sea

parts.note: St ... fire is the glow seen on ships' masts in storms, named for the patron saint of sailors

explanation.walkthrough: 'all at sea' looks like an anagram signal or 'confused', but means literally at sea, where sailors see his fire.
explanation.definitionFit: The patron saint of sailors, whose name is given to the electrical glow on masts.

clue.text: Key a bard might decipher at cock-crow

indicators.note: deciphering unscrambles a code, so the letters of key a bard are worked into a new word

explanation.surface: A poet might crack a code at dawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Cock-crow is the first light of morning, when the rooster calls.

clue.text: Perhaps a newspaper, contributing to this page

definitions.text: Perhaps a newspaper, contributing to this page

parts.words: Perhaps a newspaper, contributing to this page
parts.note: many newspapers carried this word in their titles, and those who pay for space are contributors to the printed page

explanation.walkthrough: Papers such as the Morning Advertiser bore the name, and someone who buys space contributes to the page you are reading.
explanation.definitionFit: One who pays to publicise goods; also a common old newspaper title.

clue.text: Alleged keeper with the lion of Jamshyd's courts

definitions.text: Alleged keeper with the lion of Jamshyd's courts

parts.words: Alleged keeper with the lion of Jamshyd's courts
parts.note: FitzGerald's Rubaiyat of Omar Khayyam says the Lion and a certain reptile keep the courts where Jamshyd gloried and drank deep

explanation.walkthrough: 'Alleged' because the poem only reports it: 'They say the Lion and the Lizard keep / The Courts where Jamshyd gloried and drank deep'.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Rubaiyat this small reptile is named beside the lion as guardian of the ruined Persian king's courts.

clue.text: Separate air, say, for the flowerbeds

indicators.note: say tells us the phrase before it is to be spoken, giving a word that sounds like it

parts.note: to separate is to part, and air is the atmosphere; spoken together they make a French-sounding garden term

explanation.surface: Thinning out the atmosphere between garden beds.
explanation.walkthrough: The French garden word is pronounced 'par-tair', so 'part' (separate) plus 'air' gives its sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal garden layout of ornamental beds arranged in a pattern is known by this French term.

clue.text: Share alien corn, like Hamlet " for example

parts.note: a quota is an allotted share
blé is the French word for wheat or corn, so foreign corn

explanation.surface: Dividing up foreign grain, much as Shakespeare's play might be divided into famous lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alien corn' echoes Keats's Ruth 'amid the alien corn'; here alien means foreign, giving French blé.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet is famously full of lines that people repeat and cite, such as 'To be or not to be'.

clue.text: Mountain base for gigantic assault on the gods

definitions.text: base for gigantic assault on the gods

explanation.definitionFit: A peak in Thessaly, Greece; in myth the Giants piled Mount Pelion on top of it to climb up and attack Olympus.

clue.text: Cause for tears in Rye?

parts.note: Burns's song Comin' Thro' the Rye asks: if a body kiss a body, need a body cry?

explanation.walkthrough: Rye is the field of Burns's song, not the Sussex town; the song asks whether a kiss should make anyone cry.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal or learned word for kissing.

clue.text: Pater's seen wild monster

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters of the words before it running out of control into a new order

explanation.surface: Father has spotted some savage beast.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe is ignored: the anagram of PATERSSEEN gives the hyphenated creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A huge snake-like creature of sailors' legend is a classic beast of the deep.

clue.text: A super-new America appears foreign

parts.note: a super, short for supernumerary, is a film or stage extra
neo- is a prefix meaning new
US is short for United States, America

explanation.walkthrough: 'super-new' reads as 'very new', but the hyphen hides two pieces: a super (an extra) and new.
explanation.definitionFit: Extraneous means coming from outside, not belonging, so alien or external.

clue.text: Are these ties winners ?

parts.note: put the answer in front of the word ties and you get a word for sure things, and a racing cert is a sure winner

explanation.walkthrough: The answer joined to 'ties' makes CERTAINTIES; a 'cert' is a horse sure to win, so these ties are winners.
explanation.definitionFit: Sure or definite: something beyond doubt, like a horse thought bound to win.

clue.text: Sort of university for a Cardinal Goodfellow ?

parts.note: cardinals wear red, and cardinal is a shade of red
a brick is old slang for a good, reliable fellow

explanation.surface: Which university suits a cardinal named Goodfellow?
explanation.walkthrough: A redbrick university is one of the British civic universities founded in the late 1800s, as opposed to Oxford and Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: British universities founded in industrial cities around 1900 are called this, after their brick buildings.

clue.text: Down tools, as a tent-folding Arab does?

explanation.definitionFit: Workers who walk out stop work, and a nomad who takes down a tent packs up camp; both senses of the same verb.

clue.text: Now (or almost at once) or never ?

definitions.text: Now (or almost at once) or never ?

parts.words: Now (or almost at once) or never ?
parts.note: the phrase means very quickly, and read literally as at no time at all it also means never

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase normally means 'very soon', but taken literally, at no time, it means never.
explanation.definitionFit: Very quickly or instantly; taken literally, at no moment at all.

clue.text: No roller nor bowler, this water-bearer

definitions.text: No roller nor bowler, this water-bearer

parts.words: No roller nor bowler, this water-bearer
parts.note: cricket words mislead: it is not the groundsman's roller or a bowler, but a jug

explanation.walkthrough: Cricket offers the roller (which flattens the pitch) and the bowler; this pitch word is neither, but a large jug.
explanation.definitionFit: A large jug for carrying and pouring water.

clue.text: Female deity, one Virginia barely remembered

parts.note: lady means a woman
a deity is a god
I is the Roman numeral one
VA is the abbreviation for the US state of Virginia

explanation.surface: A goddess, perhaps from Virginia, whom hardly anyone recalls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barely remembered' looks like 'scarcely recalled' but means remembered for being bare: the Coventry noblewoman who, in legend, rode naked through the town.
explanation.definitionFit: The Anglo-Saxon noblewoman of Coventry is famous for her legendary naked ride on horseback.

clue.text: What's left of vehicles that line a road

indicators.note: that points to the run of letters held within the following words, line a road

explanation.surface: Cars parked along a roadside, and what remains of them.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs through 'liNE A Road'. In Britain the left side of a vehicle is the nearside, next to the kerb, so the definition is fair.
explanation.definitionFit: British drivers keep left, so a car's kerbside left flank is called its nearside.

clue.text: Egyptian dancing-girl in German dance

parts.note: an alma or almah is an Egyptian dancing girl

explanation.surface: An Egyptian dancer performing in a German dance.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for a German dance, the allemande.

clue.text: This acid's sharp-tasting, almost acrid perhaps

parts.note: tart means sour or sharp to the taste

indicators.note: perhaps signals the remaining letters may be arranged in some other order
almost means the word acrid stops short of its final letter

explanation.surface: A chemist notes that a certain acid tastes sharp, verging on acrid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This acid's' looks like it introduces a description, but 'This acid' is the definition and the 's is 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The acid found in grapes and wine, used in baking powder, has this chemical name.

clue.text: The river serpent file?

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake

explanation.surface: Does this snake in the river crawl in single file?
explanation.definitionFit: A coarse file with raised teeth for shaping wood.

clue.text: Hang round with oil, it could become rough

indicators.note: it could become says the gathered letters may turn into a different word

parts.note: O is a round shape

explanation.surface: Hanging around with oil, things could get rough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it could become' rearranges HANG, O and OIL. 'rough' is a noun here: a rough is a ruffian.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough, as a noun, is a violent ruffian or thug.

clue.text: The flower of mixed choirs

indicators.note: mixed means the letters of choirs are stirred into another order

explanation.surface: The finest of several blended church choirs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The flower of' looks like 'the best of'; it is the definition, and 'mixed' shuffles CHOIRS.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchid, especially a wild one of a European genus, has this botanical name.

clue.text: A French lady would get up about one, in velvet-like material

indicators.note: in means that combination is placed inside the velvet-like fabric

parts.note: panne is a velvet with a flattened lustrous pile

indicators.note: about means the word for getting up goes around the letter for one

parts.note: to get up is to rise
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A Frenchwoman rising around one o'clock, dressed in velvet.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman from France's capital city is a lady of Paris.
